title: Automation keeps its tier after its accountable maintainer steps down
description: From vouch-ey47.13 review. Implemented (Claude, for Mark's review): the accountable's claim must be maintainer/anchor at the commit that added the bot's tier record (else error); if the accountable later has no valid maintainer/anchor tier, the bot's tier record is VOID (warning, check exits 0, bot has no tier until re-assigned). Alternative: pure D6 analogue, bot keeps its tier after the accountable steps down. Owner's call: is accountability ongoing (current) or judged at approval like the approver?
acceptance_criteria: Fixture: accountable maintainer's tier deleted after the bot's tier record; check passes with no void for the bot and export still lists the bot's file-namespace key. Real ssh-keygen signatures, real git history.
notes:
DECIDED (Mark, 2026-10-22): judged at approval like D6. The accountable must be maintainer/anchor at the commit that added the bot's tier record (else error, as now); if the accountable later steps down, the bot KEEPS its tier. Change current code, which voids the bot's tier record; update tests and DESIGN.md.
Review fixes (2026-10-22): accountable now gets the approver's concurrent-demotion scan (error); a bot's person file naming a different accountable than the one judged at the tier record's adding commit voids the record until a new approval (restores the protection the old final-commit check gave). Revocation outcomes pinned: revoking the accountable's own key keeps the bot; revoking the key under the accountable's tier voids it. QUESTION for Mark: should handing a bot to another maintainer be allowed without re-approval (judge the new accountable at the commit that names them)? DESIGN.md does not say; currently it needs a new tier record.
